rules.source: Ley No. 172-13 sobre Protección de Datos Personales — https://presidencia.gob.do/sites/default/files/statics/transparencia/marco-legal/leyes/Ley-172-13.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Objective: comprehensive protection of personal data in files/public registries/data banks, public or private, guaranteeing the right to honor and privacy under Article 44 of the Dominican Constitution. Published in Official Gazette No. 10737, 2013-12-15.

rules.source: Ley No. 136-03, Código para el Sistema de Protección y los Derechos Fundamentales de Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes — https://www.dgjp.gob.do/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/Ley-Nu%CC%81m.-136-03.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: The State is responsible for protecting children and adolescents against all forms of abuse, mistreatment and exploitation regardless of medium, including internet/electronic means; dissemination of images/data that could affect physical, psychological or moral development is prohibited.

rules.source: Procuraduría General de la República Dominicana — Ley 136-03 — https://pgr.gob.do/wpfd_file/ley-no-136-06/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Exposure and revictimization of children/adolescents in media is penalized under Ley 136-03; sanctions (fines and prison) established in Articles 394-411 of the Code.

rules.source: Ley General de Protección de los Derechos del Consumidor o Usuario, Ley 358-05 — https://proconsumidor.gob.do/historia/
rules.retrieved_snippet: Establishes the regime for defense of consumer/user rights, guaranteeing equity and legal security between suppliers and consumers. Enacted 2005-09-09; Article 33 recognizes rights to life/health/safety protection and truthful, clear, timely information. Enforced by Pro Consumidor.

rules.source: Ley No. 53-07 sobre Crímenes y Delitos de Alta Tecnología (2007) — https://dgii.gov.do/legislacion/leyesTributarias/Documents/Otras Leyes de Interés/53-07.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Ley No. 53-07 criminalizes offences committed against or through information and communication technologies; its considerandos state such crimes were not provided for in Dominican criminal legislation and require typification.

rules.source: Ley No. 53-07 sobre Crímenes y Delitos de Alta Tecnología (2007) — https://dgii.gov.do/legislacion/leyesTributarias/Documents/Otras Leyes de Interés/53-07.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Artículo 6.- Acceso Ilícito: accessing an electronic, computer, telematic or telecommunications system or its components, with or without another's identity or exceeding authorization, is punished with three months to one year of prison and a fine of 1 to 200 times the minimum wage (higher penalties where data is deleted, modified or disclosed).

rules.source: Ley No. 53-07 sobre Crímenes y Delitos de Alta Tecnología (2007) — https://dgii.gov.do/legislacion/leyesTributarias/Documents/Otras Leyes de Interés/53-07.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Artículo 9.- Interceptación e Intervención de Datos o Señales: intercepting, listening, recording or observing a data signal or transmission belonging to another, without prior authorization of a competent judge, through an electronic, computer, telematic or telecommunications system is an offence.

rules.source: Ley No. 53-07 sobre Crímenes y Delitos de Alta Tecnología (2007) — https://dgii.gov.do/legislacion/leyesTributarias/Documents/Otras Leyes de Interés/53-07.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Artículo 24.- Pornografía Infantil: production, dissemination, sale and any commercialization of pornographic images and representations of a child or adolescent is punished with two to four years of prison and a fine of 10 to 500 times the minimum wage; acquisition and intentional possession in an information system is also penalized (Párrafo).

rules.source: Ley No. 53-07 sobre Crímenes y Delitos de Alta Tecnología (2007) — https://dgii.gov.do/legislacion/leyesTributarias/Documents/Otras Leyes de Interés/53-07.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Ley 53-07 Artículo 17 is headed 'Robo de Identidad' and addresses a person making use of another person's identity through information technology (full text/penalty not reproduced here).

rules.source: Ley No. 53-07 sobre Crímenes y Delitos de Alta Tecnología (2007) — https://dgii.gov.do/legislacion/leyesTributarias/Documents/Otras Leyes de Interés/53-07.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Artículo 21.- Difamación: defamation committed through electronic, computer, telematic, telecommunications or audiovisual means is punished with three months to one year of prison and a fine of 5 to 500 times the minimum wage; Artículo 22 covers public injuria by the same means.

rules.source: Ley General de Telecomunicaciones No. 153-98 (1998, Gaceta Oficial 9983) — https://indotel.gob.do/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/ley-general-de-telecomunicaciones-153-98-d.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Artículo 5.- Secreto e inviolabilidad de las telecomunicaciones: communications, information and data emitted through telecommunications services are secret and inviolable, except judicial intervention under common law. INDOTEL (regulator) is reported to be reforming this law; reform not in force as retrieved.

rules.source: Ley No. 155-17 contra el Lavado de Activos y el Financiamiento del Terrorismo (2017) — https://www.aduanas.gob.do/media/lj5ikamd/ley_155-17_lavado_de_activo.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Artículo 1 (Objeto): the law establishes the acts that constitute money laundering, predicate offences and financing of terrorism, with applicable criminal sanctions, plus special investigation techniques and mechanisms (text retrieved via the Dirección General de Aduanas).

rules.source: Ley No. 155-17 contra el Lavado de Activos y el Financiamiento del Terrorismo (2017) — https://www.aduanas.gob.do/media/lj5ikamd/ley_155-17_lavado_de_activo.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Ley 155-17 title and Artículo 1(a): defines the acts constituting money laundering, predicate offences and 'el financiamiento del terrorismo', with the criminal sanctions applicable.

rules.source: Ley No. 65-00 sobre Derecho de Autor (2000) — https://www.aduanas.gob.do/media/3yndr4ja/65-00_sobre_derecho_de_autor.pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Artículo 1: the provisions of the law are of public and social interest; authors and holders of literary, artistic and scientific works enjoy protection for their works, and related rights are also protected (text retrieved via the Dirección General de Aduanas; later amendments exist, e.g. Ley 2-07 per secondary reports, not verified).

rules.source: Ley No. 74-25 Orgánica que instituye el Código Penal de la República Dominicana (2025) — https://presidencia.gob.do/sites/default/files/laws/2025-08/Ley%20Nu%CC%81m.%2074-25%20(Co%CC%81digo%20Penal%20RD).pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Artículo 192.- Difusión de audios o imágenes sin consentimiento: whoever publishes or disseminates by any means audios, images or videos of another person without consent is sanctioned (penalty begins at six months to one year in the retrieved text). Original 2025 text; later amendment Ley 44-26 reported by secondary sources.

rules.source: Ley No. 74-25 Orgánica que instituye el Código Penal de la República Dominicana (2025) — https://presidencia.gob.do/sites/default/files/laws/2025-08/Ley%20Nu%CC%81m.%2074-25%20(Co%CC%81digo%20Penal%20RD).pdf
rules.retrieved_snippet: Artículo 208.- Difamación: public imputation of a precise fact affecting a person's honor or reputation by any public means including streaming, electronic media or cyberspace; Párrafo: punished with two to five years of prison and a fine of 9 to 15 minimum salaries (original text). Artículo 210.- Injuria defines public insulting expression without imputation of a precise fact. Constitutional challenge to these articles reported by secondary sources.
